the-carnegie: The Carnegie lists gallery hours Thursday–Saturday, noon–5 p.m., and box-office hours Tuesday–Friday, noon–5 p.m. The box-office number for performance access arrangements is 859-957-1940.
Gallery Hours Thursday – Saturday Noon – 5 p.m. Box Office Hours Tuesday – Friday Noon – 5 p.m.
For specific dates and availability, please contact The Carnegie Box Office at 859.957.1940.
Tickets are final sale. Exchanges depend on availability, carry a 10% fee on the exchanged tickets’ total cost, and must be requested at least 24 hours before the performance.
All tickets are final sale. Exchanges are offered when available. Exchanges will incur a 10% fee on the total cost of exchanged tickets.
Exchanges must be requested no later than 24 hours before a performance.
ensemble-theatre-cincinnati: Ensemble locates restrooms it describes as accessible in the first-floor lobby, second-floor corridor and third-floor lobby. Of the two all-gender toilets in the Level 2 corridor, it identifies the one nearest the rehearsal-hall entrance as ADA-accessible; the Level 3 all-gender toilet is in that lobby.
Accessible restrooms are located in the first-floor lobby, as well as the second-floor corridor and third-floor lobby.
Two all-gender restrooms are located in Level 2 corridor; the one nearest to the rehearsal hall entrance is also ADA-accessible.
One all-gender, ADA-accessible restroom is located on the third-floor lobby.

Large-print programs can be downloaded as PDFs from show pages before a performance or collected at the Box Office on the day. Braille programs are available from the Box Office on the performance day.
Large-print programs Available to download in a PDF format on show pages prior to a performance and available day of the performance at the Box Office.
Braille programs Available day of the performance from the Box Office.

At relaxed performances, Ensemble keeps low-level house lights on, reduces startling/loud sound and strobe or audience-directed lighting, allows standing and movement, and permits leaving and re-entering as often as needed. It also lists designated quiet areas in the facility.

Relaxed performance modifications include: lower sound level for startling or loud sounds low-level house lights remain on throughout the performance reduction of strobe lighting or lighting focused on the audience relaxed attitude regarding noise and movement in the audience space throughout the theater for standing and movement freedom to leave and reenter the auditorium as often as needed designated quiet areas within the theater facility

For relaxed performances, additional accommodations may be requested by calling the Box Office at least 48 hours ahead. The relaxed-show page lists fidgets, noise-dampening headphones, sensory cushions and sunglasses at the Box Office; a request is not confirmation of a particular arrangement.

Fidgets, noise-dampening headphones, sensory cushions, and sunglasses are available at the box office. Patrons may request additional accommodations by calling the box office at least 48 hours ahead of the relaxed performance.

The official social narrative places the elevator in the first-floor hallway and says it goes to the third floor. Its third-floor theatre entrance has a lift beside it; confirm lift operation and assistance before choosing upper-row seating.
Also in the hallway on the first floor, there is an elevator. I can ride the elevator up to the third floor.
There is a chair lift on the third floor, next to the entrance to the theatre.

The social narrative directs visitors needing quiet time to the lobby outside the theatre and, for greater quiet, to the mezzanine, reached by the elevator’s M button. It describes chairs there; this is guidance, not a guarantee of silence or a private room.
If I need quiet time, I can go to the lobby outside of the theatre. If I need absolute quiet time, I can go to the mezzanine.
The mezzanine will have chairs to sit on or I can walk around the lobby. If I use the elevator to get to the mezzanine, I will hit the ”M” button.
The social narrative shows waiting space in the lobby and describes chairs and tables to sit at before the play. It says food and drinks bought at the bar can be taken into the theatre.
There are chairs and tables I can sit at to wait. The bar will also be open for me to buy snacks or drinks while I wait. I can bring these items into the theatre when it is time for the play.

Ensemble says the lobby opens one hour before showtime and theatre doors about half an hour before. Late seating is at the House Manager’s discretion between scenes; admission may be denied because of the production or when more than 15 minutes late.
Our lobby opens one hour prior to showtime; the doors to the theater, approximately a half-hour before showtime.

Latecomers to a show will be seated at the House Manager’s discretion at an appropriate time between scenes. You may be denied admission dependent on demands or structure of a particular production, or if you are over 15 minutes late.
memorial-hall-otr: Memorial Hall describes a separate production elevator serving the stage from the basement, Grant Street and first floor. This is distinct from the north-side patron elevator; public use, staffing and operating arrangements for the production lift need confirmation.
The stage is also accessible via the Hall's new production elevator, accessible from the basement, Grant Street, and the first floor.

The basement, first and second floors of Memorial Hall are fully accessible via the patron elevator on the north side of the building (the right side of the building when facing the front entrance), which may be entered on the street level.

Washington Park Garage lists vehicle entrances/exits on Race Street at 13th Street and on Elm Street across from Music Hall. Its pay-on-foot instructions say to take the parking ticket and pay by cash or credit card in an elevator lobby before returning to the vehicle.
Two vehicular entrances/exits are located on Race Street at 13th Street, and on Elm Street across from Music Hall.

Take your ticket with you! As you walk back to your car, stop at one of the pay station machines to pay your parking fee using cash or credit card. Pay stations allow you to pay for parking in any of the three elevator lobbies before returning to your vehicle.

The garage’s valet-assist parking program is listed for Monday–Friday, 7 a.m.–4 p.m.: enter normally and go to the second-level attendant. Regular parking rates apply without an extra valet-assist fee. This parking service does not establish passenger-transfer help or an escort to Memorial Hall.
The program will be in effect Monday-Friday from 7am-4pm

Parkers should enter the garage in the normal fashion and proceed to the second level to see the on-duty attendant. Regular parking rates apply, and there is no additional fee for the valet-assist services.
